question:
A 52-year-old male patient with a recent diagnosis of membranous nephropathy has been on Lisinopril
for the past three months. Which of the following factors would place him at high risk for progressive
disease? Answer Choices: (A) Presence of IgG4 deposits without complement activation (B) Stable
blood pressure readings averaging 130/80 mmHg (C) Proteinuria of 6 g/day at the end of the
observation period (D) Microscopic hematuria with <5 RBCs/HPF (E) A patient who is anti-PLA2R
antibody positive, with anti-PLA2R antibody titers stable at 55 RU/mL during the observation period (F)
Normal C3 and C4 complement levels with stable renal function (G) Serum creatinine elevation of 0.3
mg/dL from baseline with eGFR >60 mL/min/1.73m² (H) Proteinuria of 3 g/day with a serum albumin of
3.7 g/dL (I) Proteinuria reduction of 25% after 3 months of ACE inhibitor therapy (J) Anti-PLA2R
antibody titers decreasing to 20 RU/mL after treatment
 A. Proteinuria of 6 g/day at the end of the observation period
B. Proteinuria reduction of 25% after 3 months of ACE inhibitor therapy
C. A patient who is anti-PLA2R antibody positive, with anti-PLA2R antibody titers stable at 55
RU/mL during the observation period
D. Presence of IgG4 deposits without complement activation
E. Anti-PLA2R antibody titers decreasing to 20 RU/mL after treatment
F. Microscopic hematuria with <5 RBCs/HPF
G. Proteinuria of 3 g/day with a serum albumin of 3.7 g/dL
H. Stable blood pressure readings averaging 130/80 mmHg
I. Serum creatinine elevation of 0.3 mg/dL from baseline with eGFR >60 mL/min/1.73m²
J. Normal C3 and C4 complement levels with stable renal function
